newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo firms expect 18 pct export rise in 1997 - IZIT.
newsitem.headline: Yugo firms expect 18 pct export rise in 1997 - IZIT.

text.p: Yugoslav companies hoped for an 18 percent export growth in 1997, far below government expectations of an almost 48 percent increase in export activity, the Institute for Market Research said on Wednesday.
The government said in its 1997 economic policy paper that export growth will range between 44.4 and 48.2 percent.

"Companies' expectations seem to be more realistic because they are aware they have just a few products fit for the world market and the quality is not competitive enough," Slobodan Milosavljevic of the IZIT institute told Reuters.

Export activity will probably pick up when Yugoslavia returns to the International Monetary Fund, World Bank and the World Trade Organisation, but the return would bring new rules and standards to observe, Milosavljevic said.
"That's why Yugoslav companies expect even greater difficulties in exports than they face at the moment," he said.
Yugoslav government planned for this year a 50 percent rise in exports, but instead it recorded a sharp increase in imports and a trade gap that surged to $1.7 billion in October.

IZIT economists said trade deficit resulted from deep structural problems of the Yugoslav economy and called for restructuring so that any increase in exports contributes to bigger industrial production. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
